title: Hahn-Banach extension: witness g built from a Zorn-maximal linear graph
intent: Prove the Hahn-Banach extension theorem — every linear functional f on a submodule F' bounded by a convex p extends to a linear functional g on the whole module V bounded by the same p — by first obtaining a Zorn-maximal linear graph via zornS_ex, turning it into a function g via hahn_banach_witness, closing g's additivity/scalability with lingraphD and lingraphZ, and packing g into a {scalar V}.

parent.name: hahn_banach_extension
parent.statement:
Theorem hahn_banach_extension : exists2 g : {scalar V},
  (forall x, g x <= p x) & forall z : F', g (\val z) = f z.

children.name: zornS_ex
children.statement: Lemma zornS_ex : exists g : zorn_type, forall z, zornS g z -> z = g.
children.closed_by: apply: (@Zorn zorn_type Rbool) to the zornS order reflected as Rbool; the union graph g of a maximal chain A is shown to satisfy le_extend_graph and returned as ZornType g; the empty chain yields zphi

children.name: hahn_banach_witness
children.statement:
Lemma hahn_banach_witness :
  exists h : V -> R, forall v r, carrier g v r <-> h v = r.
children.closed_by: choice total_g gives h; the -> direction by functional_graph fg (fg v r (h v)), the <- direction by rewriting h v = r

children.name: lingraphD
children.statement: Lemma lingraphD x1 x2 r1 r2 : f x1 r1 -> f x2 r2 -> f (x1 - x2) (r1 - r2).
children.closed_by: move=> f1 f2; have := lf (-1) f1 f2; rewrite !scaleN1r mulN1r

children.name: lingraphZ
children.statement: Lemma lingraphZ x r l : f x r -> f (l *: x) (l * r).
children.closed_by: move=> fxr; have := lf l (lingraph_00 fxr) fxr; rewrite !add0r

applicability.goal_shape: exists2 g : {scalar V}, (forall x, g x <= p x) & (forall z : F', g (\val z) = f z) — a constructive existence of a structured object (a linear map g) with two properties, a bound by a convex p and an extension of f from a submodule F', from hypotheses p_cvx (p convex) and f_bounded_by_p (f <= p on F')
applicability.use_when: the witness is a structured object whose existence follows from a maximality or choice argument (Zorn's lemma, choice) followed by a short list of algebraic closure lemmas; the target properties factor into independent named lemmas (linearity, bound, extension) so the glue is a thin skeleton
applicability.avoid_when: the witness has no finite or constructible description; the object's properties do not factor through small named lemmas (each needs a bespoke argument); or the maximality argument itself is the content and cannot be isolated into one lemma

claims.claim: The glue of hahn_banach_extension (lines 308-323) references exactly four named lemmas defined in the same file — zornS_ex and hahn_banach_witness (line 310), lingraphD (line 314), lingraphZ (line 317) — and then packs g via GRing.isLinear.Build and HB.pack (lines 318-319) to close `exists2 g`.

The main proof is 16 lines (308-323) while the four children it calls total 50 proof lines — zornS_ex 38 (124-161), hahn_banach_witness 8 (279-286), lingraphD 2 (67-68), lingraphZ 2 (64-65) — so the heavy work sits in the children and the glue is a thin skeleton.

The file header states the plan and content: 'This file proves the Hahn-Banach theorem thanks to Zorn's lemma. Theorem `hahn_banach_extension` states that ... a linear function on a subLmodType of V, that is bounded by a convex function, can be extended to a linear map on V bounded by the same convex function.'

hahn_banach_extension is reused as a lemma by three later theorems in the same file: hahn_banach_extension_normed (line 352), hahn_banach_extension_subctvs (line 395) and hahn_banach_extension_initialsubctvs (line 450).

consequences: The move creates the two obligations of `exists2` (boundedness and extension) plus the linearity obligation needed to pack g as a {scalar V}; linearity is discharged by the two graph-closure lemmas lingraphD (addition/subtraction) and lingraphZ (scaling). The witness rests on the classical choice/Zorn foundation (`choice`, `@Zorn`), so the extension is non-computational. A failure mode: because lingraphD/lingraphZ are stated for a generic `linear_graph f` hypothesis, the glue must first re-establish that g satisfies linear_graph by destructuring the zorn_type spec (`case: z gP => [c [_ ls1 _ _]]`); if that spec changes shape, the destructuring breaks.
